newsitem.title: UK: UK rate rise will affect borrowing - BoE.
newsitem.headline: UK rate rise will affect borrowing - BoE.

text.p: A rise in UK interest rates last week will affect borrowing in Britain even though mortgage lenders have not put up their rates as a result, the Bank of England said on Wednesday.

"Last week's rate rise will have affected perceptions of borrowing rates over the next 12 to 18 months anyway," said Bank of England chief economist Mervyn King, at a press conference to launch the Bank's quarterly inflation report.

He said building societies rarely change their rates one-for-one with base rate changes. "But there is a fairly close relationship between mortgage rates and base rates," he said. "The rate rise will affect a whole host of borrowing rates."

King said businessmen and consumers would now expect higher borrowing rates, even though mortgage rates have yet to move. British base rates were raised by a quarter-point to 6.00 percent last Wednesday.
